title: Packaging and Cold Shipping of Human Islets
author: Integrated Islet Distribution Program
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bhdzj276
materials: The IIDP will provide each center with the supplies necessary for shipments as listed in the materials section. Standard lab supplies will be provided by the IIDP Centers as listed below.

Supplies provided by the IIDP Centers: Islets for distribution Routine lab supplies for transferring islets Completed FedEx Shipping Labels Preprinted Fresh Tissue Box Labels Islet Allocation Tissue Shipment Forms for appropriate recipients Markers for labeling vessels

Supplies provided by the IIDP: The majority of supplies should be stored in appropriate dry, temperature-controlled environments (room temperature 16°-28°C). The Prodo Labs PIM(T)® should be stored, in the dark, between 2° and 8°C upon receipt but is stable at room temperature. The Gemini AB serum and the PIM(G)® vials should be stored at -5° to -20°C in the dark. The Ciprofloxacin can be stored on the shelf but filter sterilized suspension aliquots should be stored at -5° to -20°C. Aliquots: Record media preparation on Attachment 1: Solutions Preparation Sheet : Attachment 1-Solutions preparation Sheets.pdf The Cold Chain Complete Card with the WarmMark indicator on the card and the separate ColdMark indicator can both be stored at room temperature or between 12°C to 32°C to ensure against accidental triggering of either indicator. Ice Packs and CryoPaks.
Distribute appropriate volume into shipping bottles .
Stage all materials needed for packaging the islets and ensure all ice packs and CryoPak pouches are at the proper temperature.

steps.title: Assess Islet Quality
steps.instruction: After islets recover at 37°C for approximately 18-48 hours, inspect several flasks. Isolation is ready for shipping if greater than 80% of all size islets have rounded up.

steps.title: Prepare PIM(T) Complete Media
steps.instruction: Prepare one 500 mL bottle of PIM(T) media by adding the following supplements:

substeps.instruction: Thaw and add 5 mL of PIM(G)
Thaw and add 25 mL of AB serum (5% v/v)
Thaw and add 0.5 mL of prepared ciprofloxacin sterile aliquot
Record preparation on Attachment 1: Solutions Preparation Sheet

steps.title: Collect Islets from Culture Flasks
steps.instruction: Aseptically transfer islet culture flasks from the incubator to the hood and prepare one 250 mL conical for every 6 culture flasks.

steps.title: Pool Islets into Settling Conicals
steps.instruction: Pool 6 T-175 flasks into each 250 mL 'settling' conical using a 25 mL pipette wetted with PIM(T). Repeat for all sets of flasks.

steps.title: Wash Flasks to Recover Remaining Islets
steps.instruction: Wash flasks to collect remaining islets into a separate 250 mL 'count' conical.

substeps.instruction: Deliver 20 mL of media slowly onto the bottom surface of the flask in a sweeping motion to loosen islets.
Let media run to the bottom by gravity; repeat 2-3 times, collecting the 20 mL from the bottom and delivering it to the top while rocking gently.
The same 20 mL can be used for 6 flasks by transferring the media between them.

Examine flasks under a microscope after the first wash; if many islets remain attached, deliver another 20 mL of PIM(T), gently tap the side, and rock the flask before collecting the wash into the 'count conical'.

steps.title: Transfer Settled Islets to Count Conical
steps.instruction: Allow settling conicals to rest for 10-15 minutes, then transfer islets to the 250 mL 'count conical'.

substeps.instruction: Pre-wet a 25 mL pipette with PIM(T).
Gently draw settled islets from the bottom of each settling conical using an upward movement with only ~2-3 mL of media.
Carefully deliver islets to the bottom of the 'count conical'.

steps.title: Recover Islets from Settling Supernatant
steps.instruction: Recover any remaining islets from the supernatant of the settling conicals.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the supernatant for 2 minutes @ 180 g.
Evacuate the supernatant.
Gently resuspend pellets with 2-3 mL of PIM(T) and transfer to the 'count conical'.

steps.title: Perform Islet Counting
steps.instruction: Determine the islet concentration and calculate distribution volumes.

substeps.instruction: Bring the volume in the 'count conical' up to 200 mL with PIM(T).
Invert the conical 3-4 times, then have a second technician quickly remove exactly 0.5 mL and place in a counting dish.
Place the conical horizontally under the hood while awaiting results.
Calculate islets/mL and record in the batch record (Attachment 3).
Calculate the volume needed for each shipping bottle based on the order.

steps.title: Remove Samples for Testing
steps.instruction: Remove the following quantities for quality control per IIDP protocol:

substeps.instruction: Remove 100 IEQ for Viability Test.
Remove 400 IEQ for GSIR studies.

steps.title: Aliquot Islets into Shipping Vessels
steps.instruction: Distribute islets into shipping bottles based on the total IEQ:

substeps.instruction: Use 30 mL bottle for < 10,000 IEQ.
Use 60 mL bottle for 10,000-50,000 IEQ.
Use 125 mL bottle for > 50,000 IEQ - 100,000 IEQ.

steps.title: Finalize Shipping Bottle Volume
steps.instruction: Bring the volume up to the halfway point of the bottle neck using PIM(T) stored at 6-10°C.

substeps.instruction: 30 mL bottle: Total volume 44 mL (media plus islets).
60 mL bottle: Total volume 75 mL (media plus islets).
125 mL bottle: Total volume 167 mL (media plus islets).

steps.title: Label and Store Bottles
steps.instruction: Label each bottle with RRID #, Date, #IEQ, and PI Name. Record information in the batch record and store bottles in a refrigerator at 6-10°C until packaging.

steps.title: Prepare Cold Chain Monitoring Card
steps.instruction: Prepare the Cold Chain Complete Card and indicators.

substeps.instruction: Store the Card (with WarmMark attached) at < 32°C (at least 5°C below the 37°C activation temperature).
Store the separate ColdMark indicator at > 12°C (at least 10°C above the 2°C activation temperature).
Adhere the ColdMark indicator to the card.
Activate the WarmMark by folding up and pulling out the tab until completely removed.

steps.title: Primary Packaging
steps.instruction: Seal the shipping bottles and monitoring card.

substeps.instruction: Immediately place the Cold Chain Complete Card and islet shipping bottles into a Ziploc bag and seal.
Include the Cold Chain Complete Form (Attachment 4).

steps.title: Secondary Packaging (Inner Box)
steps.instruction: Pack the Ziploc bag into the inner cardboard (S-4434) box.

substeps.instruction: Line the inner box with an absorbent pad.
Place the Ziploc bag into the absorbent pad.
Surround the bottle with six 8°C cold packs: one on the bottom, one on each of the four sides, and one on top.
Mark the direction for upright bottle, seal the inner box with shipping tape, and stand upright.

steps.title: Tertiary Packaging (Styrofoam Box)
steps.instruction: Pack the inner box into the insulated shipping container using an alternating method for packs/pouches.

substeps.instruction: Place one 8°C CryoPak pouch and one 8°C cold pack in the bottom of the Styrofoam box.
Place the inner cardboard box on top, centered and upright.
Place one 8°C CryoPak pouch and one -20°C frozen ice pack on each long side of the inner box (in the larger gap).
Place one 8°C CryoPak pouch and one 8°C cold pack on top of the inner box.
Place the Styrofoam lid on top and place the Tissue Shipment Form on the lid.

steps.title: Final Shipping and Documentation
steps.instruction: Seal the shipping container and process the shipment.

substeps.instruction: Close the flaps of the shipping box, seal with tape, and add the Box label (Attachment 6).
Attach FedEx label with recipient FedEx number and ship priority overnight.
Shipping center must enter IEQ and FedEx tracking numbers into the Islet Allocation System and alert the recipient via the on-line FedEx process.
